q: A restaurant chain wants a site where customers can book tables and order food for collection. What is the site's purpose?
why: Taking orders and bookings makes it eCommerce plus promotion — serving a clear business purpose.

q: Which layout principle means putting important content where the eye lands first?
why: Visual hierarchy arranges elements by importance so users notice key content (headlines, CTAs) first.

q: When is a hamburger menu most appropriate?
options: Mobile-first designs where space is limited
When the site has one page
why: Hamburger menus hide navigation behind an icon — ideal on small screens where space is tight.

q: Which colour pair would NOT be acceptable for WCAG colour contrast?
why: Light grey on white fails contrast guidelines — poor contrast makes text unreadable for many users. Check contrast with tools like WebAIM.

q: A client brief targets 'teenagers interested in gaming'. Which is the correct demographic approach?
options: Design for 13-19 year olds with personas for casual and hardcore gamers
Assume every user is the same age
why: Demographics plus personas let you design content, tone and visuals that actually appeal to the target users.

q: Which order should you follow when planning a new site?
options: Requirements → sitemap → wireframes → visual design → build → test
why: Understand requirements first, then structure (sitemap), then layout (wireframes), then style (visual design), then build and test.

q: You created a logo in Illustrator. Which format preserves it as a scalable vector?
why: SVG is a vector format — it scales to any size without losing quality, perfect for logos and icons.

q: Which HTML tag creates an internal link to another page of the same site?
why: Internal links use <a> with a relative href to another file in the site (about.html). <link> is for stylesheets.

q: Which CSS rule makes a website adapt to a small phone screen?
why: Media queries apply specific styles when the viewport matches, e.g. max-width: 600px for phones.

q: A tester clicks every nav link and records which work. This is:
why: Functionality testing verifies features work — links, buttons, forms. Usability testing asks real users about the experience.

q: Which is an example of publishing a website?
options: Uploading files to a web host so they are live on the internet
Saving files to a USB stick
why: Publishing means making the site publicly accessible — uploading to hosting (e.g. GitHub Pages, Netlify) with a domain.

q: After designing wireframes, why should you review them against the client brief?
options: To check they meet client requirements and improve the designs
why: The spec requires reviewing fitness for purpose — checking quality, user experience and that the designs meet the client's requirements, then improving.
